description: One slice of a TmBreakdownCard: a label, its value and an optional colour. A part carries no callback — the card is a read-only summary, and a host that needs a drill-down puts a link next to the card.

members.name: Id
members.description: Stable identity of the part, rendered as data-part-id. It is never a DOM id: a host value is not a valid id, and a slug would collide (a.b vs a-b). It should be unique within one card, because it is the row identity of the reorder animation. Duplicate and empty ids are tolerated: the card derives a private row key for a row that does not own a unique id, so every row still renders, but such a row is not tracked across a reorder (its reorder is not animated).

members.name: Label
members.description: The part's name, rendered as the row header and never only as a colour legend.

members.name: Value
members.description: The part's amount. It drives both the proportional strip and the percentage; a negative amount counts as zero for the share while the row itself stays visible, so the data is never silently dropped.

members.name: Color
members.description: Optional colour of the part, as a CSS colour value — a var(--tm-*) token reference, a hex literal, an rgb/hsl/oklch/color-mix function, or a named colour. It is written into the segment's and the row swatch's inline background-color, so it wins over the fallback token tone. A value that is not a CSS colour (a class name, or any payload carrying ;, {, } or url() emits no style and the part falls back to the rotating token tone. The same grammar TmStatCard.SubValueColor validates.
